title: Brian Chesky on Building Airbnb, Founder Mode, and Design-Led Product
speaker: Brian Chesky
description: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky shares lessons on product design, Founder Mode, scaling company culture, and why traditional divisional management fails tech companies.
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast. Today my guest is Brian Chesky, co-founder and CEO of Airbnb. Brian, welcome to the show.

Brian Chesky: Hey Lenny, thanks for having me. Great to be here.

Lenny Rachitsky: Airbnb went through a major transformation during COVID and revamped how product management and design work together. Can you share how you restructured product development?

Brian Chesky: In traditional tech companies, product management often becomes a middle-management layer that separates executives and designers from the actual product details. We got rid of traditional classic product management and combined product management with product marketing. Every product manager at Airbnb must understand both how the product is built and how it is brought to market.

Lenny Rachitsky: You also talk frequently about 'Founder Mode' vs 'Manager Mode'. What is the core difference?

Brian Chesky: Professional managers are often taught to delegate everything and inspect metrics from a dashboard. But true founders stay in the details of the product experience. Founder Mode means having deep context across key details, staying close to customer feedback, maintaining a unified design language, and refusing to delegate the soul of the product.

Lenny Rachitsky: How do you maintain high quality as Airbnb scales to hundreds of millions of users?

Brian Chesky: We treat our product as a single continuous story. Every 6 months, we do major seasonal product releases. Having fixed release cycles forces cross-functional discipline across design, engineering, and marketing. It ensures we aren't just shipping incremental button color changes, but meaningful end-to-end user improvements.
